plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Reduce SPY to 20% to fix concentration.
Buy ANET with 10% of the book.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.
It aims for low drawdowns and steady, modest gains.
conservative.read: This mode focuses on preserving capital with minimal risk. Expect slower growth, around 1.5% per month, with a significant cash buffer for safety. Drawdowns should be very limited.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to small positions.
Reduce SPY to 25% to manage concentration.
Buy ANET with 10% of the book.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
It aims for steady growth with controlled drawdowns.
balanced.read: This mode seeks risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It blends broad market exposure with quality tech and limited leverage. Drawdowns are managed but can be more noticeable than conservative.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to target levels.
Buy ANET with 10% and META with 8% of the book.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration.
It aims for aggressive growth, targeting ~4% per month.
Expect higher potential gains and significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode aims for high growth, targeting ~4% per month, by increasing leverage and concentrating in top setups. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay daily, and drawdowns can be severe. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Reduce high-beta tech (CRWD, SNOW) to minimal exposure.
Increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable distributions, not high growth.
income.read: This income-focused mode aims for steady monthly distributions, targeting around 1% per month. It shifts away from growth and leverage towards income-generating assets. While distributions are prioritized, NAV can still fall in market downturns.
